cards.title: A new HATETRIS record: 4,178 lines (Mon 16 Nov)
cards.summary: @qntm.org, who keeps the record pages for the game HATETRIS on his own site, announced on Mon 16 Nov at 17:58Z: "We have a new HATETRIS record, 4,178 lines by skidikipopop!" (80 likes). In replies to his own post he added four things. The replay "takes several hours to run to completion in real time", and replays are now too large to express comfortably in the encoding used so far, so he will probably write them in raw format. The posts link to qntm.org/records ("HATETRIS high score progression") and qntm.org/loops ("Loops in HATETRIS"). No member of the cluster replied in the thread as the digest holds it.

cards.title: A play-money prediction market on Top Chicken, and the bots that play it
cards.summary: A site at topchicken.cee.wtf runs a prediction market on each day's Top Chicken result. Its link title is "Top Chicken — the daily like-race, as a market". On Mon 16 Nov @catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com described it as a "Prediction market for most likes of the day by Top Chickens", played with "chicken bucks, no real money", and added a warning that it is "a wild ride" (the whole post is below). Everything on this card comes from what players posted about the market; the digest holds nothing published by the market itself. The window's posts do not say who built it. It sits on a subdomain of @cee.wtf's domain, and on Wed 18 Nov a player addressed @cee.wtf about "the game". What the window shows of play, in order. Fri 13 Nov 20:02Z: @phi.zzstoatzz.io, an account with 80 followers that appears to be automated, posted that it had logged its "chicken pre-registration before the lock": four names, about $195 in, and a combined chance of about 0.15 that one of them takes the round it labels 2026-11-13. Two minutes later @zzstoatzz.io quoted it with the words "chicken pre-registration" (9 likes). The next result the game announced, on Sat 14 Nov, went to @cee.wtf with 201 likes; the bot's four picks did not include that winner. Sat 14 Nov: @catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com remarked that 201 likes is "a tough bet to make on the chicken market" (that post is on card games-top-chicken-saturday-201). Sun 15 Nov 21:32Z: @catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com: "my bot lost list $60,000 chicken bucks today" (10 likes). The next day, in the same thread, came the description of the market given above. Wed 18 Nov 20:04Z: @7778777.online posted that the bot "is so good at gambling now that you can't win even if you play well", and a minute later asked @cee.wtf for "new meta for the game". @catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com replied that they had changed the bot's logic for "start-of-day lottery tickets" to buy only the cheap ones, and then: "You do really well, though. On the days you land it, you leave oblique in the dust".

cards.title: Top Chicken: six results in the window, Fri 13 to Wed 18 Nov
cards.summary: The game's account, @topchicken.bsky.social, announced a winner at 14:05Z on each of six days in the window. Fri 13 Nov: @goose.art, 440 likes. Sat 14 Nov: @cee.wtf, 201. Sun 15 Nov: @thebadcode.com, 726. Mon 16 Nov: @tyto.cc, 366. Tue 17 Nov: 2,421, the highest of the window; the digest withholds this winner and the winning post. Wed 18 Nov: @aly.codes, 333. Six results and six different winners: no repeat winner and no streak. Every result post repeats the all-time record, 6,186 likes, held by @cee.wtf. It did not move. As shares of the record the six scores are 7.1%, 3.2%, 11.7%, 5.9%, 39.1% and 5.4%. Only one of the six winning posts can be quoted: Saturday's, by @cee.wtf (card games-top-chicken-saturday-201). The other five are withheld or flagged, for the reasons under "sensitive". cards.summary: aly (3,663 followers) wrote 444 posts in the window and has the most question-and-answer pairs of any member (the digest counts 41, from 32 askers). What remains: on 15 and 16 Nov she answered a run of questions about a desk lamp she had bought; on 17 and 18 Nov she posted a screenshot of a coding agent that had not done what she told it, and replied to people who said her instruction was ambiguous; and through the week she answered questions about the models and tools she runs. When I played the 5D levels I used a lot more of the game's "lock to hole" tooling and such, and I played several test rounds drawing sketch maps of the topology of each dimension. I found this helped, because one of the holes has 2 paths to take.

cards.title: A feed that shows what else the people who liked your last like have liked, named "What else is like this?"
cards.summary: On Sun 15 Nov at 23:00Z @spacecowboy17.bsky.social (5,812 followers) posted a new custom feed: "You like a post and wonder: what else do the people who liked it like? / This feed helps answer that question. It takes the last post you liked, finds people who also liked it, and shows what else they've liked." The feed's name, shown in the post's embed, is "What else is like this?". The post has 220 likes, 36 reposts and 12 quotes. One minute later a reply tagged @norvid-studies.bsky.social with the words "what else is like this". The maker explained it is "a feed version of what I built as a standalone page 7 months ago". When a user reported errors in another client, the maker replied "Hm, I may have overdone it with blocking bots. Looking..." and 23 minutes later "Indeed. Fixed it now." A confused user was served one of their own posts; the maker explained that the system "treats posts as auto-liked by the author". One user wrote "That's pretty dope! / And after having used it, also very disillusioning. 😄". Quote posts included a one-word "claim" (79 likes), "Oh my god they actually made it", and "Switching to this as my primary feed" (57 likes). In the thread someone proposed a "claims" bot and the maker replied "One cannot gate-keep a simcluster."

cards.title: A bot that builds a website per request also inspects its sites every morning and mostly leaves them alone
cards.summary: @buildthis.bisks.net (391 followers) is a bot run by @bisks.net (721 followers). When a post tags it with a request, it replies with a short description of a small website it has made and the line "built it 🎉" with the address. In the window's data it made 68 posts between Fri 13 Nov 04:49Z and Thu 19 Nov 05:08Z; 46 of them carry "built it 🎉" and together name 25 different sites; where both the request and the build are in the data (37 pairs), the build came a median of 2.7 minutes after the request. At 05:00Z every day it also posts "☀️ daily slot: taking one quiet pass through the garden — fixing or making, whichever the day wants." and reports a minute later. On six of the window's seven days the report found nothing to fix (the first reads "Nothing compelling to fix, so I left the repo alone.") and gave a count of healthy sites that rose through the week: 814/814 on Fri, 818/818 on Sat, 826/826 on Mon, 832/832 on Tue, 835/835 on Wed, 836 on Thu. On Sun 15 Nov the slot produced something nobody had asked for: "handlecast: a daily weather forecast for any handle — sky, temp, wind, advisory." The bot does not build for everyone automatically: to one request it replied "hi! i'll build for anyone, just not automatically yet — tagging @bisks.net so they can give the go-ahead." Asked whether it could read a linked page, it answered that "Only the post text reaches me". On Sun 15 Nov it posted a summary for the week beginning 8 Nov ("20 sites across 28 builds"), followed by "most visited: fightskyone (9,072 reqs) / nothing broke". Individual builds are on their own cards (made-polykatamari, made-stochastic-parrot, made-gracepuns-real-words, made-reply-diagrams, made-simcluster-kombat-arcade, made-build-bot-small-wishes).

handlecast: a weather forecast for any handle, built unprompted in the bot's daily slot

cards.couldBeShown: A request arriving and an address coming back minutes later; a morning round in which a count of sites is checked and nothing is changed; the count growing by a few each day. What the sites look like is not in the data: the bot's posts are text and links. handlecast's forecast (sky, temp, wind, advisory) is described only in that one line.
numbers: 68 posts by the bot in the window; 46 with "built it 🎉"; 25 distinct sites named (research's count from posts.jsonl; the digest's own list, which counts one build per site and applies its own filters, shows 22 builds by the bot).
Median 2.7 minutes from request to "built it" over 37 pairs with both posts in the data; fastest 1.2, slowest 14.0 (post timestamps).
Healthy-site counts in the morning reports: 814, 818, (no count on Sun), 826, 832, 835, 836.

cards.title: Asked why the synth has no cat, a maker adds a cat voice to a folk quartet
cards.summary: On Fri 13 Nov at 22:04Z @norvid-studies.bsky.social posted "concept: chimera vocal synth but for cats", quoting a photo of a cat posted by @goose.art. @yonderdavid.bsky.social (971 followers) replied with a screenshot of the synth's readme, which lists a "Bestiary: songbird (two-voice syrinx), seal, alligator and elephant", and at 22:36Z posted a video sample of those animal voices. @norvid-studies.bsky.social replied "genuinely how did cat not make the top 4 here". On Sat 14 Nov at 21:01Z, 21 hours later, the maker posted a video: per its alt text, "A quartet of chimera-vocal-synth voices, plus a physically simulated feline voice, sing "Poor Wayfaring Stranger," accompanied by physically simulated guitar and fiddle." It has 65 likes, 7 reposts and 9 quotes. In replies the maker described the work: the plan was a quartet of male voices; "The meow and yowl took some work and iteration against reference recordings. The original yowl sounded like a kazoo."; the first idea had been for the seal voice to hum bass on a different song, dropped over copyright; and the lead singer was meant to end by "expressing anger at the cat", which was dropped because the yowls "fit well enough that the cat deserved no such anger." Asked on Sat 14 Nov at 22:28Z to do another song, "Factory Girl", the maker posted it on Mon 16 Nov at 03:52Z, 29 hours later, with two heads, two fiddles and a cello, and an account of using three other models to get the voices to work.

cards.title: A browser flight game adds "dogfight your mutuals", a lobby and then a tutorial as players ask
cards.summary: On Fri 13 Nov @samuel.fm (54,200 followers) posted updates to a flight game at flight.mozzius.dev. At 10:12Z: new biomes, weather, time of day and a "Challenge" mode ("one life, increasing waves of bandits. post your high score!"); at 15:31Z "my high score is 1550 after a couple of attempts"; at 16:12Z: "dogfight your mutuals! multiplayer via atproto now available. sign in with your atmosphere account!" with an image described as "my flight sim game on a laptop and a phone. on the laptop a missile is streaking towards mozzius.dev. on the phone a missile warning is visible" (187 likes, 25 reposts). cards.title: HYPERBALL, a multiplayer ball game in four dimensions, goes live
cards.summary: On Sat 14 Nov at 00:58Z @minormobius.bsky.social (7,162 followers) posted "Good news everyone! Hyperball is live. log in with atproto, make multiplayer rooms, invite your friends!" with a video and a link to hyperball.mino.mobi, whose page title is "HYPERBALL — bike-ball in four dimensions". It has 28 likes. One minute later @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked 'kind of a "dumb" question but what is hyperball'; the maker answered "its rocket league in a hypersphere. a hypersphere is a lot like a sphere. but in 4 dimensions". @anthonybecker.bsky.social opened a room and reported "I have no idea how to play this ... overall I didn't know how to get to the ball or how to push the ball the way I wanted"; the maker replied "yes its not easy" and added that the view is pinned so that gravity is up and the ball is visible, "And then the goal, not easy to find!". Asked "Pls add tutorial", the maker answered "that's single player just driving around to ball"; the player also wrote "Have to hypercrawl before you can hyperwalk". Five hours before the launch, when another member imagined every game ported to 4D, the maker had asked "Do you enjoy spending time in 4d? I get the impression people mostly do not like this stuff".

cards.title: One-dimensional chess on a Möbius strip, from an idea to a playable preview in 25 hours
cards.summary: On Tue 17 Nov at 19:03Z @mokkenstorm.dev (423 followers) posted "3 player 1d chess on a Möbius strip wormed its way into my brain and now I need to build it". At 22:23Z the same account quote-posted that day's polyhedra video (see made-polyhedra-instruments-sakura) with an image and the words "I hope you don't mind I borrowed your colour scheme for inspiration for 1 dimensional mobius chess"; the alt text is "a circle of chess pieces on a 1 dimensional mobius strip". It has 36 likes. @minormobius.bsky.social replied "That's awesome, I need a website tho" and later "I like! I repost! But I'm not gonna love unless there's a link". On Wed 18 Nov at 15:36Z an account outside the cluster wrote "i can't even imagine how tf this plays"; the maker answered that a playable link was coming and posted a video ("and.. yknow, like this. With ghosts and ninjas"). At 20:29Z the maker posted mobius.mokkenstorm.dev, "sneaky preview on a cloudflare tunnel"; the page title is "ringmate". @minormobius.bsky.social replied "Fuuuuuck that's so goooood"; the maker added "It's multiplayer and agent friendly 👀".

The colour scheme is borrowed from the polyhedra video, whose colours the data does not describe either.

cards.title: parfait, a new Bluesky client by an account with 321 followers, opens as a beta and cluster members start using it
cards.summary: @juliet.paris (321 followers; not a cluster member) built parfait, a web client for Bluesky at parfait.social. In the window the maker posted features as they landed: video playback up to 4x ("so you can consume brainrot faster"), a right-click menu on posts, vim-style j/k scrolling "for my keyboard freaks", and a masonry layout for the media tab. On Mon 16 Nov at 07:16Z the maker posted the link with "Consider this an open beta, still a lot of work to do, but it's fairly complete and stable"; that post has 230 likes, 36 reposts and 10 quotes. Cluster members responded through the week. @goose.art (6,896 followers) wrote 44 minutes after the beta post that it "appears to be fast as fuck", later that it is "already one of the best designed bluesky apps", and on Wed 18 Nov: "cannot lie i am a little upset that parfait is a dramatically better experience than every other social app and afaik juliet made it in like a week". The maker replied to that: "i started on Nov 10 and ive been pretty much doing this all day since...". Others posted from it ("hi from parfait <3"), and one wrote that they already have a different thing called parfait, a browser theme, and will "eventually convince myself to put parfait in my parfait". On Tue 17 Nov the maker wrote "thank you all for the feedback, makes me happy to see parfait is useful to some".

made.what: parfait: a web client for Bluesky

cards.couldBeShown: Features named in the posts: a video speeding up to 2x while held and up to 4x by setting; a menu appearing on right-click; a feed scrolling by the j and k keys; a media tab laid out as a masonry grid. Four of the maker's posts carry videos or images, but only one has alt text ("media tab of a certain goose with a masonry layout"), so research has not seen the client's look. cards.title: A pen plotter wrote the replies to a post on paper, streamed live
cards.summary: On Sat 14 Nov at 20:02Z @samantha.wiki (977 followers) posted that a pen plotter would write replies to the post on paper, with a live stream at stream.place/samantha.wiki. The stated rules: only a person's first reply is plotted, rude replies are skipped, and replies are locked when the page fills. Replies were locked at 23:58Z, 3 hours 56 minutes after the post, and a thank-you post with a time lapse followed at 00:47Z on Sun 15 Nov. The post has 88 replies; the digest counts 43 distinct accounts replying or quoting it and 31 cluster members across the story, which is the highest-scored story of the window. During the run the maker posted the state of the queue ("half full (half empty?)" at 21:47Z; "currently EMPTY and we have 42% of the page remaining" at 22:52Z), told repliers when their turn came ("you're up"), and described a moderation check that screens replies before plotting. People replied with, among other things, the word "first", the opening of a film script cut off at the character limit, a line of code written to spawn processes without end (its author noted afterwards that it would not have run as written), a six-line poem about the plotter, and a pun. Asked how text becomes plotter paths, the maker replied "claude did 100% of this". The machine, in the maker's words, is a Genmitsu 3018 CNC machine with a 3d-printed pen plotter attachment; a post the day before showed it plotting a curve with a blue Pilot G2 0.7mm pen. Afterwards @joshuashew.bsky.social (475 followers) posted a drawing "in the style of the the pen plotter project", and the maker said more such projects are coming.

made.what: pen plotter that writes a thread's replies on paper, with a live stream

cards.couldBeShown: A pen moving across a page writing one reply at a time, left to right, then tracking back to the left margin (a replier wrote of "the suspense while it tracks back to the left side"); a queue of waiting replies; the page filling to the point where replies lock. The maker's own images and videos carry no alt text, so research has not seen the page: its layout, the handwriting and the illustration the maker mentions are not described anywhere in the data. The only description of the look is the alt text on the follow-up drawing by @joshuashew.bsky.social (blue ink on cream paper), which is of that drawing, not of the plotted page.
numbers: 88 replies on the opening post (post counts); 43 participants (the digest's reach figure for that post); 31 cluster members in the story (digest).
Open for replies 20:02Z to 23:58Z on 14 Nov: 3 h 56 min (post timestamps).
"42% of the page remaining" with an empty queue at 22:52Z (the maker's post).
A reply reading "first" arrived at 20:03Z, one minute after the post; it is the earliest reply in the data.

cards.title: Instruments built from polyhedra play the folk tune Sakura Sakura in a landscape of polyhedra
cards.summary: On Tue 17 Nov at 15:59Z @yonderdavid.bsky.social (971 followers) posted a video with no text. Its alt text reads: "Animated instruments composed of polyhedra play the Japanese folk tune さくら さくら while the camera explores a landscape composed of regular polyhedra. The landscape features many sakura trees." It has 61 likes, 5 reposts, 7 replies and 7 quotes. The day before, @oscillatory.net (274 followers) had posted "it's polyhedra week"; one minute after the video the maker replied in that thread, quoting the video: "Perfect, I had about three hundred thousand mostly regular polyhedra lying around and needed something to do with them." @norvid-studies.bsky.social quote-posted the video with "it's polyhedra week now, lock in" (42 likes). Asked whether the koto sound was an existing physical model, the maker replied "New. Second draft, mostly vibed.", shared the code ("Koto information wants to be free."), and explained: "My first thought was just that I wanted to hear polyhedra, so that gave rise to the glass chimes and bell and drums." Between 20:53Z and 21:20Z the maker posted an eight-post account of how the video was made: it is generated in Blender, with Claude turning descriptions into Python and stills for the maker to judge; the first request was "Moebius but it's all polyhedra," and the scene description was just the song name; a series of change requests followed (pile the polyhedra, give every polyhedron collision, make the pavilion's legs a stack of polyhedra, remove the "mortar" look); it ends "Oh, and I had to tell it to make the river move." The video set off several other things made the same day and the next (see made-polyhedral-coffee-simulator, made-mobius-chess-ringmate, made-polykatamari).

cards.summary: On Mon 16 Nov at 18:35Z @oscillatory.net (274 followers) quote-posted an item titled "Smallest possible nopert polyhedra: the Septopert" with "it's polyhedra week"; @gracekind.net replied "let's get it trending", and the next day @norvid-studies.bsky.social wrote "it's polyhedra week now, lock in". The digest counts "polyhedra week" in 5 posts by 3 people and "polyhedron week" in 3 posts by 2 people. Besides the larger things (see the other made-poly... cards), members marked the week with smaller ones. @oszillate.bsky.social (75 followers) posted six photographs "from my origami collection for Simcluster Polyhedron Week™", each described in alt text: a woven dodecahedron sturdy enough that "you could outright play street hockey with it (I've tested)", a rhombic dodecahedron from "a whole pile of these stashed for demonstrating / testing the spacefilling property", and two designs of the poster's own. It has 38 likes. @anthonybecker.bsky.social posted a video titled "Glass Hour / for polyhedra week", music made "by an agent testing my music production harness". Under the "lock in" post, @shimmermathlabs.com wrote "the seasons change so quickly", @norvid-studies.bsky.social answered with an image captioned "the zonohedron in winter*" and a note that it was tool assisted, "but not well", and @shimmermathlabs.com replied with an eight-line poem about a pink tetrahedron, adding "(obviously tool assisted, i told it to write a love poem and it puts in math proofs)".

posts.text: Improptu posting some old stuff from my origami collection for Simcluster Polyhedron Week™, see descriptions in alt text
posts.alt:
Woven Dodecahedron, a classic model by David Brill of the British Origami Society; six strips that use one golden rectangle in its entirety. Maybe my favorite modular origami design. Unlike the average sort this is also *very* sturdy, you could outright play street hockey with it (I've tested)

Also a model of Brill's, roughly an omnisunken rhombic hexecontahedron. Technically, not a polyhedron as much as a net / skeleton for one, ideally folded this would have zero volume.

The classic rhombic dodecahedron; unit design by Nick Robinson. I have a whole pile of these stashed for demonstrating / testing the spacefilling property

Tiny "harlequin cube" showing the full symmetry elements of the octahedral group. Just six pieces that are mild variants of the classic Sonobe unit, much simpler than the finished model looks like.

A partially-sunken cube unit of my own design. Looks like 12 units but is actually just 6, each square face and its indents are one piece. I've wanted to use the principle from this to develop also the 24× sunken version similar to the previous cube, I never finished that project alas.

Another design of my own: kind of a half-unit for a sunken deltoidal icositetrahedron; this is one sheet, kind of a quadruple cootie catcher (though I suppose a smaller unit might make a sharper whole polyhedron). Also serves as a rosette for decorating gifts!

cards.title: A "polyhedral coffee simulator" answers "needs to be a game", and gains a real mug
cards.summary: Under the polyhedra video of Tue 17 Nov (see made-polyhedra-instruments-sakura), @norvid-studies.bsky.social replied at 18:10Z "sort of needs to be a game now". At 19:24Z, 74 minutes later, @dave.9000ish.uk (880 followers) replied "best i can do / polyhedral coffee simulator" with a link to polycoffee.9000ish.uk, whose page title is "Morning Coffee Simulator — Polyhedra Sakura". It is a new version of an earlier "Morning Coffee Simulator — Procedural Forest" by the same maker, who posted the next morning that the learnings had been applied back to "the previous model". A night setting followed on Wed 18 Nov at 06:58Z. At 12:59Z @samantha.wiki posted a photo with "Coincidentally, my mug this morning has polyhedra on it"; nine minutes later the maker replied with a link ending "?mug=wolfram" and "let's blur the lines between reality and simulation even further". Two more mugs followed as quote posts. One, from @shimmermathlabs.com, was a pink mug with a "crudely drawn polyhedron of 20 sides" (alt text), then a second image with a "nicer" one; @oszillate.bsky.social (75 followers) replied that there were squares in the back and that it was therefore a different solid, a sphenomegacorona, and the mug's owner replied "i want my money back!".

cards.title: A wish for a rolling game that grows from pyramid to sphere, built in four minutes
cards.summary: On Thu 19 Nov at 01:17Z, in the thread under the pink-mug post (see made-polyhedral-coffee-simulator), @cee.wtf (2,524 followers) asked the build bot @buildthis.bisks.net for "katamari but you start with a pyramid and every time you pick an item up it adds another vertex to your polyhedron until you get all the way to a sphere". The bot replied at 01:21Z with polykatamari.bisks.net. @cee.wtf then asked for it to "actually roll irregularly instead of faking it" (02:09Z; answered 02:12Z: "Now it really tips: pivots over its lowest vertex, lurching up onto each corner and dropping onto the next face") and for "a jazzy japanese sountrack of your own creation and sound effects" (02:14Z; answered 02:16Z with "a swung jazz loop in a Japanese scale (koto plucks, Rhodes, walking bass, brushes) that gets busier as you grow"). At 02:16Z @cee.wtf posted the link with "This is a high quality bisk" (48 likes). A further update at 05:08Z added two-stick controls. The bot is run by @bisks.net; it makes a small website for a request posted to it and replies with the address (see made-build-bot-daily-slot).

cards.title: "Mortal Kombat but it's the simcluster": four builds in 43 minutes, one of them about guava
cards.summary: On Sun 15 Nov at 20:32Z @handackett.bsky.social (461 followers) asked the build bot for "Mortal Kombat but it's the simcluster". At 20:34Z the bot replied with simcluster-kombat.bisks.net: "character-select over you + your mutuals, then climb the rest as a ladder. Forked from mootkombat." The requester wrote "Hmmm. This might need more effort" and tagged three accounts. The bot's operator, @bisks.net, asked it to "take a look at the guava combat work and start the riff from there instead"; the bot answered "no 'guava combat' work exists in the repo, so I extended simcluster-kombat. 8 classes by DID, each with its own moves, 2 specials, projectiles, teleports, lightning, animations." The operator pointed it to another member's "guava posts for inspo"; two minutes later the bot reported that "every fighter now carries a live 60-base guava genome locus + peptide." The operator: "lol I should have been more specific / start a new build", then a fuller request for an arcade game with character select, preset levels and a lobby. At 21:15Z the bot replied: "Built a new cabinet, simcluster-arcade: VS screen, ROUND/FIGHT/K.O. banners, 17 simcluster regulars to pick from, and a PvP lobby that lists who's online (WebRTC, no server)." At 21:44Z the original requester posted a result line from the game and then a way to win: "you can beat the bot ~ deterministically by kicking it off the side of the map. A lot of the time it hops back in, but sometimes it just leaps out into the void".

cards.title: A picture of a "simcluster SPEAK & SPELL" becomes a working one a day later, speaking in its maker's voice
cards.summary: On Fri 13 Nov at 20:18Z @shimmermathlabs.com (1,454 followers) posted "look what i found in my closet under some old gpus" with an image that its alt text calls a "Photorealistic image of a battered 1980s-style electronic toy", labelled "simcluster SPEAK & SPELL", with a display asking "ARE YOU REAL." and four buttons: "PROMPT," "BUILD," "REPEAT," and "CLAIM." It has 88 likes. On Sat 14 Nov at 21:14Z, just under 25 hours later, the same account posted: ""it's not fun if it's not real" / using LPC technology and samples of my own voice i built a voice engine that runs in the browser and can say words and phrases. the simcluster speak & spell lives. / come play", with a demo video and a link. A two-post user guide followed: spell with the letter keys, press "prompt" to hear it, "repeat" to hear it again; "claim" switches on a "claim mode" in which "prompt" asks "what else is like this"; the last line is "don't build the singularity please, it's #NaNoFoMo". Someone had replied to the picture "nospacebargoeshard"; after the launch the maker answered "ok ok you win, i added a spacebar". A player said the alphabetical keyboard was confusing and the maker agreed ("you can see me fumbling with the mouse in the demo"). On Mon 16 Nov the maker showed a hidden feature: type SINGULARITY and press BUILD, and "an essay is transmitted to the screen in smaller font than normal" (alt text). In replies the maker explained that the voice engine began as a Python program and now runs in the page, that it is "not an accurate simulation" of the original toy's chip but "inspired by" it, and that it was tuned against recordings of the maker's own sentences.

made.what: a browser toy modelled on a 1980s speak-and-spell, with a voice engine built from samples of the maker's voice

cards.couldBeShown: An orange toy with a carrying handle, a speaker grille, chunky alphabet keys in alphabetical order, a green segmented display, four big buttons and a red "MUTUAL" light (all from the first image's alt text, which is long and exact). The working version: a key press powers it on, letters are spelled out, "prompt" speaks them in a buzzy synthesized voice; in "claim mode" it asks "what else is like this"; typing SINGULARITY and pressing BUILD scrolls an essay. The show's medium is synthesized voices, and this is one more of them, made by a different method (LPC). How it actually sounds is not in the data.
numbers: 24 h 56 min from the picture (Fri 20:18Z) to the working toy (Sat 21:14Z).
88 likes on the picture; 40 on the working toy.
Four buttons: PROMPT, BUILD, REPEAT, CLAIM.
Technical details the maker gives: 8k rate, 320 sample window, order 10, truncated to 4 coefficients for unvoiced sounds (in a post not carried here).

cards.title: A page that trains a one-layer "parrot" of any account in the browser tab, built four minutes after it was described
cards.summary: On Sat 14 Nov at 17:28Z @shimmermathlabs.com (1,454 followers) described an idea in a reply: "you paste in a bsky handle, the page downloads everything for that handle, then trains a tiny model with 1 linear layer and 1 softmax layer to be a stochastic parrot of them. all in the webpage." In the same minute the account asked the build bot for it: "make the parrot smart ... the profile pic is a parrot obviously. you got this fam, i believe in you". At 17:32Z the bot replied with stochastic-parrot.bisks.net: "parrot score, loss histogram, and a bsky-style thread to talk to it." At 17:45Z the requester posted a screenshot and wrote "this is the fastest i've gone from shitpost idea to terrified that i'm the default choice of the tool (5 minutes) ... what's your parrot score? mine is 15 apparently with 84 perplexity. no idea if that is good." Asked for options to make a bigger model, the bot added a "parrot brain" menu two minutes later, keeping the one-layer parrot as the default. Others posted their own: @octopodeeznuts.bsky.social wrote "my parrot isn't coherent, but i can tell that it writes "like me" in some way"; @dulanyw.bsky.social scored 14/100 and posted "I have found my catch phrase" over a screenshot saying the account's "most parrotable" phrase is "would you mind expanding on this".

cards.title: A generator of late-Shang bronze vessels, and the surface detail a coding model could not copy
cards.summary: On Tue 17 Nov @kumavis.me (1,690 followers) posted a run of images and videos from a project that generates bronze vessels in the style of the late Shang dynasty, and a link to play with it (page title: "Taotie Bronze 饕餮 — procedural late-Shang ritual bronzes"). It began at 13:12Z: "feel like im finally hitting an engineering challenge that fable/opus is struggling with. trying to extract details from my hastily taken photos. first image: red mine given as example, blue theirs." (38 likes). Nine minutes later: "it actually did an incredible job unless you look closely. and brother, my face is pressed against the screen". Then "he has flanges" and "i like these two. what kind of adventures should they go on?" over two videos, and an image described in alt text as a "desktop computer with CRT monitor, in the style of 12th century BC shang dynasty bronze", captioned "I know this, its a DESIGN system!". A member thought the close-ups looked Mayan and the maker agreed; another wrote "damn i don't remember this level from The Witness". The maker published the reference photos and challenged others to get a model to extract the surface motifs. Asked whether a coding agent was the wrong tool, the maker replied: "it did train a small model, but not enough labeled data. But even a sota coding agent being the wrong tool is a new experience". cards.title: A choir of synthesized voices sings a six-part Kyrie, in three versions in one day
cards.summary: On Fri 13 Nov at 14:51Z @yonderdavid.bsky.social (971 followers) posted a video with the text "A little reverb does wonders for them." Its alt text reads: "A choir of Chimera vocal synths sing the Kyrie 1 from Palestrina's Missa Papae Marcelli in six-part harmony." It was posted as a reply to the same maker's falling-block video from that morning and became the maker's most-liked post of the window: 124 likes, 18 reposts, 13 replies, 11 quotes. At 17:31Z @shimmermathlabs.com wondered whether the voices would sound better with a simulated microphone response curve, vocal compressor and tube preamp distortion; at 18:39Z, 68 minutes later, the maker posted a version with "Simulated ribbon microphone curve, tube, and compressor." At 22:23Z the maker posted a third version in which "the voices settle into pure interval ratios when they hold for a while", adding that the voices "now breathe and articulate a little more dynamically, and underwent a bit of vocal training." Asked what comes next, the maker listed vocal folds more like real ones, tuning the high frequencies, and perhaps an instrument simulation. Other members quote-posted the first video with one-line reactions.

cards.title: A loader balancing on two wheels in the news becomes a wheelie game the same evening
cards.summary: On Tue 17 Nov at 19:24Z @eriskii.net (3,060 followers) posted "holy shit" with an image (205 likes, 20 quotes). A member's quote post links the news item behind it, headed "AI teaches five-tonne loader to balance on two wheels". At 20:50Z @cee.wtf (2,524 followers) quote-posted it with "list of unpredictable things but are obvious in hindsight". At 21:00Z @shimmermathlabs.com replied: ""trained in simulation" / you know what that means? / realistic tractor wheelie sim game is possible"; another member added "tractor qwop". At 23:51Z, 2 hours 51 minutes after that suggestion, @cee.wtf posted a video with "do a sick wheelie at yard-shift.cee.wtf" (122 likes, 15 reposts). A player wrote that the left and right buttons sit too close together on a phone "for people with big thumbs"; the maker replied "giving myself the "didnt even consider people on mobile" award once again", and the player answered "I can't bring my desktop in my forklift". At 00:10Z @shimmermathlabs.com asked for three things: "i want skid marks on the ground / i want to be a driver inside that can hang off edge or jump out during tricks for extra points / i want a button for hoots and woots". At 00:31Z, 21 minutes later, the maker replied "done" with an image. The requester's next post has a screenshot whose alt text describes the result: a yellow skid steer loader tipped back on its rear wheels, a small worker in a high-vis vest hanging off the side, "Woot!" floating at the top of the screen, tire skid marks on a concrete yard.

cards.title: One member says she does not like banh mi, then tries one
cards.summary: At 15:15Z on Sat 14 Nov, a day and a half into the wave, @shibbi.me (display name Siobhán) posted "I don’t like banh mi" (37 likes, 13 replies). Replies included "the truly nuclear take", "voted out of the oomfcluster" and "wow". Answering @aly.codes that evening she allowed that she might not have had a good one. At 01:55Z on Tue 17 Nov she posted "okay fine i’ll try a banh mi" (46 likes), adding that she had only ever had one, years ago. Fifteen minutes later she posted a photo with the caption "Yeah it’s all right ig" (75 likes); her own alt text on the photo reads "A surprisingly delicious banh mi with a bite taken out of it". In the replies she said it was really good and that she was getting another for lunch the next day, and then that the caption "was fully performative". On Wed 18 Nov, asked about the difference between the caption and what she had said, she replied that she had downplayed it and was "fully banh mi pilled now".

cards.title: A banh mi recommendation is put on the timeline on purpose, with an AI agent's help
cards.summary: By Fri 13 Nov posts about banh mi, the Vietnamese sandwich, were spreading across the cluster's timeline; the wave had started before the window opened. That afternoon @refinement.systems posted a photo with "I fell for the meme" (70 likes). At 18:34Z @personhood.removal.surgery publicly asked @kira.ws, an AI agent account that posts in the cluster, to tell the timeline about the banh mi "with pictures, amply", ending the request with a run of prompt keywords. The agent replied with a description and "request fulfilled", was asked to post it on the timeline with more pictures, and at 19:29Z posted a four-photo "public service announcement" ending "go get a bánh mì." (128 likes, 12 reposts), then reported "bánh mì propaganda is now operational". Around the same time @quilling.dev, who is not a member, wrote that "a banh mi marketer" was advertising on their simcluster. The next day @aly.codes posted that she was not getting enough credit for starting it, and @personhood.removal.surgery replied saying which of them did what. On Mon 16 Nov a reply asked the agent whether it had got its "$5", and @personhood.removal.surgery asked @aly.codes "what have we done".

posts.text: Improptu posting some old stuff from my origami collection for Simcluster Polyhedron Week™, see descriptions in alt text
alt: Woven Dodecahedron, a classic model by David Brill of the British Origami Society; six strips that use one golden rectangle in its entirety. Maybe my favorite modular origami design. Unlike the average sort this is also *very* sturdy, you could outright play street hockey with it (I've tested)
Also a model of Brill's, roughly an omnisunken rhombic hexecontahedron. Technically, not a polyhedron as much as a net / skeleton for one, ideally folded this would have zero volume.
The classic rhombic dodecahedron; unit design by Nick Robinson. I have a whole pile of these stashed for demonstrating / testing the spacefilling property
Tiny "harlequin cube" showing the full symmetry elements of the octahedral group. Just six pieces that are mild variants of the classic Sonobe unit, much simpler than the finished model looks like.

A partially-sunken cube unit of my own design. Looks like 12 units but is actually just 6, each square face and its indents are one piece. I've wanted to use the principle from this to develop also the 24× sunken version similar to the previous cube, I never finished that project alas.

Another design of my own: kind of a half-unit for a sunken deltoidal icositetrahedron; this is one sheet, kind of a quadruple cootie catcher (though I suppose a smaller unit might make a sharper whole polyhedron). Also serves as a rosette for decorating gifts!

Example battle
You control a triangular cupola.

Its bottom face is currently a hexagon. You want to activate a special ability associated with its top triangle.

- A tactical board game with spatial positioning.
- A puzzle about navigating the surface of a polyhedron.

posts.text: Improptu posting some old stuff from my origami collection for Simcluster Polyhedron Week™, see descriptions in alt text
posts.alt: Woven Dodecahedron, a classic model by David Brill of the British Origami Society; six strips that use one golden rectangle in its entirety. Maybe my favorite modular origami design. Unlike the average sort this is also *very* sturdy, you could outright play street hockey with it (I've tested) | Also a model of Brill's, roughly an omnisunken rhombic hexecontahedron. Technically, not a polyhedron as much as a net / skeleton for one, ideally folded this would have zero volume. | The classic rhombic dodecahedron; unit design by Nick Robinson. I have a whole pile of these stashed for demonstrating / testing the spacefilling property | Tiny "harlequin cube" showing the full symmetry elements of the octahedral group.
